# 1.2.32 - the pulse back, and the sidebar out of the curtain's way

**The glass breathes again.** The pulse stopped in 1.2.30 and the cause was
in two places. The pulse and seam layers are created after `mount()` writes
its positioning, and nothing positioned them - an unpositioned canvas is an
inline box in flow, and the half-size pulse layer wrapped onto a second line
under the screen. In 1.2.27 a watchdog re-mount on a GM's screen happened to
stamp the positioning on afterwards, which is the only reason the pulse was
ever seen. And a rebuild that recut the same geometry replaced the pane
objects with fresh ones - without the phase and period `curtainPaint` gives
them - and then, because nothing had changed, did not repaint: the pulse read
undefined phases, computed NaN, and drew nothing from then on. 1.2.30 recuts
on every drift, so that took effect at once. Every layer is positioned the
moment it exists, and an identical cut keeps its painted panes. Verified on
a page carrying the module's markup with Foundry stubbed: the layer paints,
the alpha moves between samples, the self-check is clean.

**The sidebar does not exist for the curtain.** The rule changes. Opening the
sidebar moves nothing and recuts nothing: the glass is the screen, always;
the right-hand column is pinned where it stands with the sidebar closed, its
`right` measured from the tab rail so Foundry's paddings need not be known;
and an expanded sidebar slides over the strip and the tray instead of pushing
them. The wall, its two attempts at detecting the sidebar, the collapse hook,
the `transitionend` listener and the sidebar's part in the drift signature
are all gone.

`audit/glass-harness.html` is the page the fixes were measured on: serve the
repository root and open it, and the curtain mounts without Foundry.
